question: What does a staged curriculum need, and is generalization inherited?
answer: A ladder chains only under four conditions, and the full task then works where only its low stages were trained.
details: RL from scratch in a toy world: a point gripper moves a cube onto a target, 8 rounds, 5 to 10 seeds per recipe. Stages must be prefixes of the task, each new step its own stage, outputs unsaturated, old stages replayed success-only. A flat hand-shaped reward is still more reliable on the whole workspace; the ladder's gain is inheritance.

question: What can RL from scratch learn in the arm sim?
answer: Reaching and descending, yes. Grasping stalls and lifting is unsolved. The inheritance test was not readable.
details: PPO from scratch on the SO-101 scene with state inputs (no camera), scored on held-out placements, one seed per run. The staged ladder got further than flat RL on the same reward. The run meant to test inherited generalization under-learned, so it shows nothing either way.

question: Do the big models work on the tuned ACT recipe?
answer: SmolVLA went from 2/30 to 14/30 on the new recipe, and 19/30 after RL (not analysed). Half-trained pi0.5 got 7/30.
details: pi0.5 and SmolVLA fine-tuned on the tuned ACT baseline's data and scene (SO-101, physics v2, 100 mm lift, execute 30). SmolVLA's gain is the recipe, not better placement: it still closes 13 mm off. pi0.5 was cut to 5,000 steps and its loss was still falling.
